app.name: LinkedIn
app.canDo: Sign users in and post for them. With partner approval, manage company pages, ads and recruiting.

verdict.summary: After an admin of your company Page confirms your app, you can sign people in and post for them without approval. For company pages, ads, sales and recruiting, LinkedIn must approve you as a partner.

whoYouNeed.role: An admin of the LinkedIn Page of your company
whoYouNeed.why: Each developer app connects to a LinkedIn Page. A Page admin must confirm that connection.

whoYouNeed.role: A person who can describe how your business will use the API
whoYouNeed.why: Partner programs ask what you will build. The higher tier needs a screen recording.

steps.title: Sign in to the LinkedIn Developer Portal
steps.plain: Sign in at linkedin.com/developers with your LinkedIn account.
steps.whyHuman: You must sign in yourself. You must also accept the LinkedIn API terms yourself.

steps.title: Create the app and connect your company Page
steps.plain: Create a new app. Give it a name and a logo. Select the LinkedIn Page of your company.

evidence.note: Third-party guides give the Page requirement. The LinkedIn docs that we read do not say it clearly.

steps.title: Get a Page admin to verify the connection
steps.plain: In the Settings of the app, click Verify next to the Page. Generate a link. Send the link to a Page admin for approval. The link expires after 30 days.
steps.whyHuman: Only an admin of the company Page can approve.

evidence.note: Third-party sources do not agree. Some say that each Page admin can approve. Others say that only a super admin can approve.

steps.title: Add the self-serve products
steps.plain: On the Products tab, add 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn'. These products need no approval.
steps.technical: These products give openid, profile, email and w_member_social. With w_member_social, the app can post, comment and react as the member.

steps.title: Add the callback address and copy the credentials
steps.plain: On the Auth tab, add the callback address of your app. Then keep the client ID and secret in the secret store or environment variables of your app.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is the password for your app. Paste it yourself. Then it does not go into the chat history of an agent.

steps.title: Apply for Community Management API (only for company pages)
steps.plain: Do this step if your agent posts for company pages or reads their analytics. Apply for the Community Management API. Start with the Development tier. Then apply for the Standard tier with a screen recording of each use case.
steps.whyHuman: The application describes your business and how you will use the API. LinkedIn then examines your company.

steps.title: LinkedIn examines your application (company pages only)
steps.plain: LinkedIn reviews the request for the Development tier. Then it reviews the upgrade to the Standard tier. LinkedIn does not publish how long the reviews take.

evidence.note: LinkedIn gives the two tiers and the review. LinkedIn gives no time. The range of days is our estimate.

steps.title: Apply to the partner program (ads, sales or recruiting)
steps.plain: Each area has its own program. For ads, add the Advertising API product on the Products tab of your app. For sales or recruiting, apply to the Sales Navigator (SNAP) or Talent partner program.
steps.whyHuman: LinkedIn reviews your business and how you will use the API.

steps.title: LinkedIn reviews your partner application
steps.plain: LinkedIn does not publish how long partner reviews take.

evidence.note: LinkedIn gives the programs. The wait is our estimate.

steps.title: You cannot read the posts of a person
steps.plain: LinkedIn does not accept requests for r_member_social now. You cannot get this access. Design your agent so that it does not need it.

forks.condition: Your agent works with ads, Sales Navigator or recruiting
forks.effect: Each area is a different partner program with its own application: Advertising API, SNAP or Talent. LinkedIn reviews your business. A form is not sufficient.

forks.condition: Your agent must read the posts of a member (r_member_social)
forks.effect: This is closed. LinkedIn does not accept requests for this permission.

nuances.title: Community Management needs a new app
nuances.detail: You can request the Community Management Development tier only on a new app. The app must have no other API products. This is why the request button can be gray.
nuances.ifStuck: Create a second app for the application. Connect it to the same Page.

nuances.title: Development tier limits
nuances.detail: The Development tier allows 500 requests for each app and 100 for each member. This page does not give the time period.
nuances.ifStuck: Get the Standard tier before you launch to real users.

nuances.title: API versions expire
nuances.detail: LinkedIn publishes a new version of its marketing APIs each month. Old versions stop on a set date. For example, the November 2025 version stops on November 16, 2026.
nuances.ifStuck: If calls fail after an end date, find the API version that your code sends.

config.redirectUriNote: Add your HTTPS callback address on the Auth tab of the app.

scopes.name: openid profile email
scopes.plain: Sign the person in. Read their name, photo and email.

scopes.name: w_member_social
scopes.plain: Post, comment and react as the person.

scopes.name: w_organization_social
scopes.plain: Post as a company page. This needs Community Management approval.

useCases.label: Sign people in, or post as the person who connected
useCases.summary: These products need no approval. Do steps 1 to 5.

useCases.label: Post for company pages, or read their analytics
useCases.summary: Community Management API. LinkedIn examines you for the Development tier. Then you need a screen recording for the Standard tier.

useCases.label: Ads, Sales Navigator or recruiting
useCases.summary: Each area is a different partner program. LinkedIn reviews your business for each.

evidence.note: LinkedIn gives the programs. LinkedIn publishes no times. The wait is our estimate.

useCases.label: Read the posts of a person
useCases.summary: Closed. LinkedIn does not accept requests for r_member_social.

version.note: This is not OAuth 1.0a. You do not sign each request.

flow.note: The token request needs the client secret.

pkce.note: LinkedIn must turn it on for your app first.

callback.note: Use HTTPS and an absolute URL. LinkedIn ignores query parameters, and # is not allowed.

tokens.note: Refresh tokens are only for some partners.

state.note: If it does not match on return, send 401 Unauthorized.

composio.note: Users can connect today through the Composio LinkedIn app. Use it while you set up your own app or wait for the review. Users see 'Composio' on the approval screen. Other Composio customers share the same rate limits. Polling triggers run a maximum of one time in 15 minutes. Change to your own app when it is ready. LinkedIn Ads is a different Composio toolkit. It needs your own app.

limits.note: The Composio LinkedIn docs list actions for company pages. They do not say if the Composio app has the permissions for company pages. Also, you cannot put some permissions together in one app. Make sure before you use it for company pages or partner APIs.

evidence.note: The toolkit page shows that Composio has its own app. It does not show the permissions of that app.

existingApp.summary: If the callback address of your agent is different, add it on the Auth tab of your app. Use the existing client ID and secret. The products that LinkedIn approved stay on the app.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You want Community Management on an app that has other products
reReviewTriggers.effect: LinkedIn accepts Community Management requests only from a new app with no other products. Create a second app. Connect it to the same Page.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You need a new partner product (ads, sales, recruiting)
reReviewTriggers.effect: Each product needs its own application and approval. This is also true for an approved app.

blockers.symptom: LinkedIn refuses your request for Community Management
blockers.cause: LinkedIn examines these items: how you will use the API, a verified business email, your organisation, its website and domain. A super admin of your company Page must verify the app. Personal email addresses fail.
blockers.fix: You cannot apply again with the same app. Correct the problem. Create a new app. Send a new request for the Development tier.

blockers.symptom: LinkedIn refuses your upgrade to the Standard tier
blockers.cause: These are the usual causes: the screen recording did not show each use case on your form, the privacy policy was missing or not valid, or the app breaks the LinkedIn data storage rules.
blockers.fix: Record a clear screen recording with a voice explanation. Show only your app and show each test case. Then create a new app and send a new request for the Development tier. You cannot apply again with the same app.

authorize.detail: Sign-in endpoint answers and rejects a made-up app ID: "Authorize LinkedIn LinkedIn The passed in client_id is invalid oauth-guides-check-not-a-real-app"
